messages.author: 512610f4917ceaf3
messages.subject: Compiling Rstan under clang++ (c++11)
parts:
Hi,

Has anyone tried to install Rstan with 'clang++ -std=c++11 -stdlib=libc++' in R-devel on a Mac?

Thanks,
Rob J. Goedman
goe...@icloud.com

--------- DETAILS -------------

Following the standard route (CRAN builds, etc.) I have no problem with using Stan or Rstan.

Compiling stan with clang++ also works fine and finishes 'make o=0 test-unit' without any problems.

But recently I have been looking into compiling R and Rcpp, RcppArmadillo and RcppEigen using clang++ with the 2011 extensions. Rcpp, RcppArmadillo and RcppEigen all work and indeed I can compile lambda functions, say using Rstudio or using command line R on my Mac.

The next step was to try and compile Stan and Rstan using the same compiler flags.

The command line version of stan does generate, in addition to the 'warnings' I'd seen with just clang++, 'notes'  (e.g. lib/boost_1.53.0/boost/concept_check.hpp:521:15: note: in instantiation of member function),  but seems to work in the end (see stan-output.txt below, all the way at the end and sample.csv), although 'make o=0 test-unit' now fails (see test-output.txt).

Installation of Rstan produces similar error messages as making stan for command line usage, but now will fail as illustrated in bernoulli.txt.

I couldn't figure out how to present an easier, reproducible example.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Compiling Rstan under clang++ (c++11)
parts:
On Sunday, June 23, 2013 8:22:52 PM UTC-4, Rob J Goedman wrote:
The command line version of stan does generate, in addition to the 'warnings' I'd seen with just clang++, 'notes'  (e.g. lib/boost_1.53.0/boost/concept_check.hpp:521:15: note: in instantiation of member function),  but seems to work in the end (see stan-output.txt below, all the way at the end and sample.csv), although 'make o=0 test-unit' now fails (see test-output.txt).

You have to add -DBOOST_RESULT_OF_USE_TR1 to CFLAGS in the makefile. Even with that, test-unit will probably eventually fail for Stan v1.3.0, but it does pass on the origin/develop branch from Github as long as you don't try values of O_STANC greater than the default of 0.

Ben

I said the wrong option. You actually need to add -DGTEST_USE_OWN_TR1_TUPLE to CFLAGS_GTEST in the makefile.

Ben

parts:
Hi Rob,

Sorry for the delay. I don't have any insights into getting clang++ to work with rstan, but here are some things that might help:

- test-output.txt:
add an additional compiler flag -DGTEST_USE_OWN_TR1_TUPLE. That will get you past not being able to build test/gtest.o
- Rstan-output.txt: the error looks suspiciously like something went wrong inside ~/Projects/R/R_projects/Rstan/8schools/8schools.R. Can you attach that file? It looks like the schools code may be incorrect.
- bernoulli.txt: so the source file looks ok (it uses bivariate.R), but I think the Stan compiler (stanc) may not have been built properly. If both the 8schools and the bernoulli examples don't parse, something is going on.

Can you set the compilation flags to O=3? This is starting to look like a Windows issue where the Stan compiler can't be built at O=0, but that's the best guess I've got.



Daniel

On Tuesday, June 25, 2013 4:58:55 PM UTC-4, Rob J Goedman wrote:
I've attached 8schools.R below, but haven't changed that file for a while now and it runs fine with Rstan using CRAN R-3.0.1.

I'll try what happens with other levels of optimization when compiling stan.

What surprises me is:

1)        Compiling stan and installing Rstan both create error messages as below (related to templating in the boost package?).

2)        But while stan works, e.g. the standard bivariate example in src/models/... works fine, Rstan can't compile a 'similar' input file (bivariate.R, added below) with the console displaying:

If the parser (stanc) is compiled with optimization and you use C++11, then there will be a parser failure along the lines of what you found. There is some debate about whether this behavior is a bug on boost's part. Command-line Stan has O_STANC distinct from O so that you can compile stanc without optimization and the rest of stan with optimization. But rstan uses one optimization level for everything.

Maybe rstan 2.0 will make this distinction. But for now, if you want to use C++-11, you are pretty much stuck with command-line Stan. However, Stan doesn't use any C++-11 features, so I doubt it would have a noticeable effect on performance. We've been trying to get compliant with the C++11 standard for a while but mostly to make sure that we don't have any undefined behavior.

Ben

On Tuesday, June 25, 2013 10:21:11 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
Yikes.  I didn't realize it didn't work as opposed to just
issuing a warning.

It works if stanc is not compiled with optimization, which is the default for command-line Stan. RStan has never done different optimization levels for stanc and the rest, because it either used what was in ~/.R/Makevars or did -O3. With the most recent version of R, we can actually behave like Stan does.

But I can't think of a reason why an RStan user should care about using --std=c++11 anyway.

Ben

>>> It works if stanc is not compiled with optimization, which is the default for command-line Stan. RStan has never done
>>> different optimization levels for stanc and the rest, because it either used what was in ~/.R/Makevars or did -O3.
>>> With the most recent version of R, we can actually behave like Stan does.
>>>
>>> But I can't think of a reason why an RStan user should care about using --std=c++11 anyway.
>>
>> Agreed. For another project I want to use Rcpp/RcppArmadillo with C++11 extensions and ran into the issue.
>>
>> Your and Bob's answers confirmed the behavior I noticed. Compiling Rstan with -O0 indeed solves the issue!

parts:
Bob,

A couple of weeks ago we exchanged some emails about this subject and you suggested to see if this is a 'stan' problem or possibly in the Boost Spirit Qi (BSQ) parser. Some testing confirmed it is a parsing issue. Under O_STANC = 3 even the very first "data {..." was not recognized.

To make this problem reproducible, I ended up simplifying it all the way down to 2 grammars, a program-grammar and a whitespace-grammar which still show the problem. The resulting 'simplfied' source tree can be found at https://github.com/goedman/clang11-spirit-qi .

The whitespace-grammar is identical to the one used in Stan. The simplified program-grammar has very little to do anymore with Stan's syntax (but you'll recognize it :-).

It parses fine under O = 0, but differently under O = 3 (update line 7 in the Makefile). Under O = 3, it does not recognize 'prog {' etc. (see program.txt in the source tree).

Assuming the simplified source tree is in a directory ./stan-qi-problem and that is the current working directory of a Terminal, I do:

clear && rm parser && make parser && ./parser program.txt

I believe you mentioned that an email has gone out to the BSQ team but no response has been received. If you think it is useful to proceed with this investigation I could try to post this reproducible source tree to the BSQ team to see if that helps in getting a response (I know the tree is still more then a single main program, but testing goes pretty fast now).

A further request is whether a few list members can check this on their systems. On my MacbookPro I use below clang++ version:

Robs-15inch-2:stan-qi-problem rob$ clang++ --version
Apple LLVM version 5.0 (clang-500.1.63) (based on LLVM 3.3svn)
Target: x86_64-apple-darwin12.5.0
Thread model: posix

It would be nice to know if this is clang, clang version and/or Mac specific.

Regards,
Rob J. Goedman
